deities: Baba Sodal (child deity of the Chadha clan, believed an avatar of Sheshnaag; worshipped as a cobra idol at his samadhi spot)
festivals: Sodal Mela on Anant Chaturdashi (September - Punjab's biggest Hindu fair, 1.5-2.5 lakh devotees)

history.period: Over 100 years old (per local belief - verify)
history.summary: Dedicated to Baba Sodal, a child deity of the Chadha clan who, per legend, drowned himself in a pond at this site after his mother's angry words, then appeared as a holy snake to announce his farewell from the mortal world; a cobra idol is worshipped at the samadhi spot. Devotees consider him the third avatar of Sheshnaag (after Lakshman and Balaram). The annual Sodal fair on Anant Chaturdashi (September) draws 1.5-2.5 lakh pilgrims and is described as Punjab's biggest Hindu fair. The founding date is undocumented beyond local tradition.

name: Sodal Mandir
town_description: Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, named in legend after the demon Jalandhara, and a major Doaba-region commercial and industrial centre on NH-44. The Baba Sodal shrine stands on Sodal Road near the Devi Talab Mandir, close to the city centre. It is one of the city's most visited Hindu shrines, drawing over a lakh devotees for its annual September fair.

travel.airport: Adampur domestic airport (~25 km, limited service - verify); Amritsar international (~80 km - verify).
travel.road: On Sodal Road near Devi Talab Mandir in Jalandhar city; NH-44 passes through Jalandhar; auto/taxi within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: September for the Sodal Mela; October to March for pleasant weather.
